mentions.text:
HOLY $SHT is up +30%⚡ today.

The news: Smart High-Tech is accelerating industrialization. First target is production capacity of at least 1 million pads per month, driven by demand from AI, data centers, advanced semis, and electrification.
Read that again. One million pads a month. This is the ramp question I flagged finally getting an answer.

$SHT makes graphene-enhanced thermal interface material. The layer that pulls heat off a chip. As GPUs get bigger and hotter, the old two-layer TIM stack cannot keep up. SHT built the single-layer replacement. The chips outgrew the old solution. SHT built the new one.

Why I hold conviction, in order:

The progression is real and documented. Huawei prototype orders in 2022. AMD choosing GT-TIM for datacenter chips in 2024, volume, in the public record. Thermal Grizzly shipping into 90-plus countries. Then Henkel, climbing from MOU to strategic partner to approved TIM supplier. Three years of stepping up from development company to commercial company.
Henkel is the tell. Over $20B in sales. A company that size does not enter a strategic partnership with a Swedish micro-cap, commit capital, and put the Loctite brand on the material unless it sees a very large commercial opportunity. They do not attach that brand to a science project.

The NVIDIA angle: ot an official press release but take the hint.The company's own shareholders' presentation names it directly: "Direct Nvidia relationship, rare access for a company this size." "Founder-Chairman with deep technical mastery and Nvidia's confidence." And the number that matters: SHT today meets roughly 10% of potential NVIDIA demand. That is a ~10x gap. Data center cooling is called NVIDIA's fastest-growing material need. Not a material need. The fastest-growing one.

The hard catalysts. First delivery to a world-leading AI hardware company on May 25. End-customer approval passed. A $300K prepayment inside a $5M 2026 framework. And now the move to industrialize toward a million pads a month.

The bet was always one question: can they manufacture at scale? Today they told us they are building for exactly that.

The risk is the same question from the other side. $SHT has stumbled on production before. Scale it and the upside is extreme. Miss the ramp and that is the ceiling. Add dilution, capital is needed and a directed share issue already drew governance concerns at the AGM.

The balance take:

The technology is validated. The partnerships are real. A $20B partner is putting its brand on the line. The founder is pointing at the biggest customer in AI hardware. First deliveries are out the door. That is asymmetric.

But this is a micro-cap, a unkown one at that. Execution kills this bet, and unproven ramps break more often than they deliver.

So size it for what it is. This is a MOONSHOT so for me that means MAX 2% of the book, I won't add more, I won't sell, this is a 2030 bet, not one I'm trying to profit from next week.

Positioned before the ramp proves out, not after.

This name is just getting started.

I'm long $SHT ⚡
